text:
jane_support: FYI customer (Acme) says /v1/rerank (batch mode) is returning scores that don't line up with the candidate lists when they send large batches. They say the top scores appear shifted one candidate over for ~30% of queries.

jane_support: minimal repro from customer attached, they batch ~48 queries with variable candidate counts. payload snippet:
```curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/rerank -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-xxx' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"queries": [ {"id":"q1","input":"foo","candidates":["a","b","c"]}, {"id":"q2","input":"bar","candidates":["x","y"]} /* ... total 48 queries ... */ ]}' ```

laura_ml: can you paste the x-request-id from the failing request and a tiny captured response showing the misalignment? need concrete example to repro.

jane_support: request header showed x-request-id=req_0abc123. here's a tiny condensed example they extracted (real payload larger):
```request: {"queries":[{"id":"1","candidates":["A","B"]},{"id":"2","candidates":["C","D","E"]}]}
response: {"results":[{"query_id":"1","scores":[0.72,0.12]},{"query_id":"2","scores":[0.95,0.44,0.21]}]}```
But customer observed that score 0.95 actually corresponds to candidate "A" from query 1 (they saw A get top result in UI). so it looks like one or more candidate lists got concatenated and indices shifted during chunking.

omar_eng: thanks. hypothesis: rerank batcher does chunking by total candidates (chunk_size=256) and we may be failing to reset the per-query offset when a chunk boundary splits a query list or when multiple queries share the same chunk. if the offsets aren't applied correctly when we stitch results back, you get cross-query leakage.

omar_eng: quick repro plan: craft 6 queries with candidate counts [100,110,60,50,30,40] so total > 256 and see if any scores map to previous query. also try varying chunk_size via internal config (can reproduce locally).

laura_ml: if customers need a short-term workaround: 1) send smaller batches (<= 16 queries) or 2) set per_query_mode (send one query per request) or 3) ensure each query candidate_count <= 200. please pass these options to Acme for now.

sarah_cs: telling Acme now, offering to split their requests server-side while we investigate. creating INC-4321 and linking the request-id.

jane_support: Acme prefers us to handle on our side if possible — they're hitting it from a streaming job and can't easily change their client.

omar_eng: understood. I'll open a tracker and prototyping PR. rough patch: ensure chunker emits (chunk_id, query_local_start) per-query and stitch uses absolute offsets. also add unit tests specifically for query-splitting boundaries.

omar_eng: tagging eng-ml and eng-runtime — pinging @laura_ml for verification once I have repro logs.

laura_ml: can you drop the failing raw server log lines (showing candidate_count and chunk assignments) here when you have them? will validate scoring pipeline.

deploy-bot: rerank-batcher/canary deployed (rev: rerank-batcher@canary-2026.03.15) — no traffic routing changes yet.

omar_eng: I'll run the local repro against canary and post results. if it reproduces, we do quick rollback or patch.

sarah_cs: customer updated, noted mitigations and that we're actively debugging. asked for a narrow SLA exemption to allow server-side splitting while we fix.

jane_support: thanks all — keeping ticket INC-4321 open. will follow up when we have a confirmed repro or hotfix.

(attachments: condensed payload example, request-id header, customer screenshot showing candidate->score mismatch)
